cards.headline:
Frankfurt 2026: from content
to trusted knowledge
cards.body: At Frankfurt 2026, one product lead kept asking how trusted content becomes useful knowledge in AI-driven workflows.

blocks.x: Hong Zhou, VP of Product Management at KnowledgeWorks Global, left Frankfurt Book Fair 2026 with more questions about how we use AI than about what it can do. His recurring question: how do we turn trusted content into useful knowledge, and help people act on it?

As AI breaks publications into smaller pieces, a claim is only useful if its evidence, limitations and context stay attached. Publishers should rethink which metadata are mandatory for downstream reuse and reproducibility.

AI discovery needs a permission and value model, not just a technical connection. A working connector does not guarantee content gets selected: the question is not just “Can AI reach our content?” but “When and why will it choose to use it?” Zero click need not mean zero value.

Trust was one of the most-heard words. Kudos’ findings: roughly a third of respondents begin searches through AI tools or search engines featuring AI answers, and 40% mistakenly believe search-engine AI overviews are human-created or curated.

On agents, he urges starting with a specific problem and defining success, failure and exceptions before increasing autonomy; counting deployed agents tells us little. Frankfurt’s key message, for him, was about the connections around knowledge: between a claim and its evidence, a use and its permission, and an automated action and the people responsible for it.
